objective: Implement the sim-header-v1 /ws adapter with explicit subscribe/unsubscribe acknowledgements, ping/pong, bounded non-blocking fan-out, initial snapshots, gap-observable event sequences, and the allMids, l2Book, trades, and user-filtered orderUpdates subscriptions.

assertions: Tests cover subscribe acknowledgements, unsubscribe acknowledgements, ping/pong, initial snapshots where specified, and updates for allMids, l2Book, trades, and orderUpdates.
orderUpdates requires X-Sim-User at upgrade and never leaks another local user's snapshot or events; public subscriptions do not require user identity.
Snapshot/event sequencing lets a client detect gaps, and a full or lagging subscriber cannot block the single-owner engine or other subscribers.
Unsupported subscription and WebSocket post-request variants fail explicitly instead of silently approximating Hyperliquid behavior.
The adapter uses only shared snapshots/events/commands and adds no oracle ingestion or matching behavior.

deliverables: WebSocket control and subscription adapter under crates/sim-server/src/ws
WebSocket integration fixtures including slow-subscriber and user-isolation tests under crates/sim-server/tests/ws
risks: Initial snapshot and event handoff can lose or duplicate updates without an explicit sequence boundary.
Slow consumers can create backpressure on matching or unbounded memory growth.
Incorrect user routing can disclose synthetic account activity across simulator users.
notes: WebSocket post requests are outside the frozen MVP profile. The task relies on task #2 to pre-establish sim-server dependencies and module exports, avoiding overlap with the HTTP task.
